title: The Blaschka Object Network — Upstream Living-Specimen Supply Register
scope: Sources for living marine organisms and other biological reference material moving into the Blaschka workshop before glass models moved outward. The register treats acquisition, forwarding, survival in transit, revival in aquaria and failed supply as part of model production rather than external background logistics.
network_observation: The workshop depended on a reverse circulation: fragile living reference organisms moved inward to Dresden, where they could be observed in aquaria, before durable but fragile glass representations moved outward to museums and teaching collections.

actors.name: R. T. Smith
actors.role_label: aquarium/marine-specimen supplier and natural-history exchange participant
actors.identity_guard: Initials are preserved. No fuller personal identity is assigned without independent evidence.
actors.role_guard: Leopold Blaschka's draft correspondence describes Smith as an aquarium dealer. Hardwicke's Science-Gossip independently shows R. T. Smith in Weymouth and, from 1874 onward, at the exact 25 St. Alban's Street address circulating slides and marine material. This supports a commercial/exchange role but does not by itself establish a formal incorporated firm.

workshop_evidence.source: Leopold Blaschka to R. T. Smith, draft, notebook of draft correspondence 1880–1885, LRBC MS 0013 Box 23
workshop_evidence.evidence: Published archival citation identifies an order timed for weather favourable to anemone fishing and forwarding, showing that season and transport conditions entered the procurement decision.

workshop_evidence.source: Leopold Blaschka to R. T. Smith, draft, notebook 1886–1887, LRBC MS 0013 Box 23
workshop_evidence.evidence: Published archival citation identifies continuing requests for small consignments of living anemones from Weymouth.

workshop_evidence.source: Leopold Blaschka to R. T. Smith, undated draft, notebook 1886–1887, LRBC MS 0013 Box 23
workshop_evidence.evidence: Published transcription reports weakness after arrival and four specimens that did not revive, possibly after night frost on the railway.

A draft headed to R. T. Smith, Weymouth requests British sea anemones worth about 15 Reichsmarks, specifies preferred varieties, asks for as many different kinds as possible, and asks Smith to propose a forwarding method. The same draft contrasts this with marine animals previously received from Italy.

A draft headed 'Mr. Smith Weymouth 17. Mai' reports that anemones arrived alive and recovered immediately in the workshop tank despite very warm weather and several days in transit from Weymouth to Dresden. The draft then discusses previous packing failure and a new test consignment, making packing practice part of the live-animal supply experiment.

Leopold recalls having received Smith's address several years earlier as an aquarium dealer and asks for an alternative Devon supplier for Caryophyllia Smithii because it could not be obtained in Weymouth; he explicitly asks for an address from which marine animals could be forwarded in small quantities as Smith had done.

independent_contemporary_network_evidenc.source: Hardwicke's Science-Gossip, project document D118, page-level record R43088
independent_contemporary_network_evidenc.evidence: R. T. Smith, Weymouth offers larvae in exchange for good microscopic slides. This is the earliest exact-name occurrence currently isolated in the microscopy corpus and shows Smith participating in exchange before the address-bearing notices.

independent_contemporary_network_evidenc.source: Hardwicke's Science-Gossip, project document D125, record R44448
independent_contemporary_network_evidenc.evidence: R. T. Smith, 25 St. Alban's Street, Weymouth offers well-mounted microscopic slides of marine algae, forty varieties, plus small unmounted starfish for good slides.

independent_contemporary_network_evidenc.source: Hardwicke's Science-Gossip, project document D125, record R44496
independent_contemporary_network_evidenc.evidence: The same name/address offers microscopic slides of marine algae and starfish plus small unmounted starfish for good slides.

independent_contemporary_network_evidenc.source: Hardwicke's Science-Gossip, project document D125, record R44688
independent_contemporary_network_evidenc.evidence: The same name/address offers named, well-mounted marine-algae slides for mounted sections of the human body, showing repeated participation rather than a single advertisement.

independent_contemporary_network_evidenc.source: Hardwicke's Science-Gossip, project document D120, record R43515
independent_contemporary_network_evidenc.evidence: R. T. Smith, 25 St. Alban's Street, Weymouth offers Bulla hydatis and other material for mounting palates in exchange for good slides, plus palates and jaws of Gyrodus. The exchange repertoire therefore extended beyond algae and starfish.

contemporary_collector_list_ambiguity.source: William R. Hughes, On the Principles and Management of the Marine Aquarium, paper read 1874, published 1875
contemporary_collector_list_ambiguity.evidence: A list of marine-animal collectors, said to be taken principally from W. A. Lloyd's handbook, contains an OCR reading 'E. J. Smith, 25, St. Alban's Row, Weymouth.' The address is strikingly close to the repeated R. T. Smith Science-Gossip address, and the context is explicitly suppliers of marine animals.
contemporary_collector_list_ambiguity.guard: Do not merge E. J. Smith with R. T. Smith yet. The initials and Row/Street wording require image-level verification against the 1875 printed page and, if possible, Lloyd's underlying list. This may be OCR error, a related person at the same address, or a separate collector.

research_value: connects Blaschka model-making to British amateur microscopy and exchange networks
shows living reference organisms as logistics-dependent research material
makes weather, season, rail transit duration and revival in aquaria part of production history
allows comparison between circulation of mounted marine slides, unmounted specimens and living animals
creates a person/address bridge across two otherwise separate project corpora
shows a repeated exchange practice over at least 1873–1876 rather than a one-off encounter before the Blaschka supply correspondence
next_actions: Align all five exact R. T. Smith microscopy records to page images and preserve original typography/address forms.
Run exact-name search across all Rakow OCR records and align each Smith draft to manuscript page/image.
Build one chronological table of requested species, price, weather, dispatch method, transit duration, survival and subsequent model references.
Verify the Hughes/Lloyd collector-list initials and address against page image before entity merging.
Search Weymouth directories and census/address records only to resolve identity, keeping business-role evidence independent of genealogy.

parallel_supply_routes.evidence: Rudolf Blaschka's 6 January 1896 account to George Lincoln Goodale states that the workshop's seawater tanks contained living animals sent partly from the Imperial Austrian Zoological Station at Trieste and partly from England and northern coasts.
parallel_supply_routes.research_use: Institutional comparator to Smith's small-scale commercial/exchange route.
